artifacts.summary: Six-phase plan to deploy the source store, hand-remove the stale install-once mcp__lean-lsp__* grant, and verify baseline-relatively against the pre-deploy findings set.

memory_candidates.content: Install-once deploy artifacts invert the source-store-deploy boundary rule. In this repo, .claude/ is normally a disposable regenerable deploy artifact, so hand-edits there are wiped by the next deploy and the source-store-boundary rule forbids them. But files listed in loader.lua's INSTALL_ONCE_ROOT_FILES (settings.json, settings.local.json) are copied only when absent and are excluded from unload deletion, which makes them effectively user state: a redeploy will NEVER overwrite them. Consequence: a stale entry in an install-once file is structurally unfixable by redeploying and MUST be hand-edited in the deployed tree, even though the advisory source-store-boundary hook will fire. The correct response is to record the install-once reasoning in writing (summary and change log), not to silence the hook by editing the already-correct source copy. Corollary for rollback planning: install-once files are the one part of .claude/ that a re-deploy cannot restore, so they need an explicit backup before any hand-edit.
